title: Classes as Blueprints
summary: Understand what a class really is: a reusable blueprint or template. Learn how to write your own class with properties and behaviors.
learningObjectives: Understand the core definition: a class is a blueprint or template
Identify properties (fields) and behaviors (methods) inside a class
Write a clean Java class declaration from scratch without fear
expectedOutcomes: Clear understanding that writing a class does not create an object yet
Ability to write a valid class blueprint with fields and methods in Java

activities.title: The Architect's Blueprint vs The Real House

analogy.headline: You cannot sleep inside an architect's paper drawing
analogy.story:
Before an architect builds a house, they draw a blueprint on paper.

The blueprint describes everything the house will have: 3 bedrooms, 2 bathrooms, a front door, and a garage. It also describes what the house can do: turn on lights, open doors, ring doorbell.

Can you sleep inside that paper blueprint? Can you park your car in it? Of course not! It is just a plan — a description.

To live in a house, a construction crew must use the blueprint to construct the actual physical building of bricks and wood.

In Java:
- **Class** = The Blueprint on paper.
- **Object** = The Real House built from that blueprint!
analogy.keyTakeaway: A class is a design template that describes what properties and behaviors an object will have. The class itself is not the actual object.

activities.title: Anatomy of a Java Class
A Complete Blueprint Example: The Book Class
activities.description: Observe how natural the Book blueprint is. Any book in the world has a title, an author, and a number of pages. The class simply groups these related attributes into a clean, reusable blueprint.

questions.prompt: When you write 'class Dog { String name; void bark() { ... } }', does a real dog exist in computer memory yet?
options: Yes, Java immediately creates 10 dogs automatically
No, you have only written the blueprint/template for what a Dog should look like and do
Yes, but only if the file is saved with the name Dog.exe
No, classes can never create objects in Java
questions.explanation: Writing a class is like drawing an architectural plan. No actual object is created in memory until you explicitly create one (using the 'new' keyword).

hints.hint: Think about the house blueprint analogy.

questions.prompt: Inside a class, what do variables (like 'String name;') and methods (like 'void study();') represent?
options: Variables represent memory addresses; methods represent compiler warnings
Variables represent properties/data; methods represent behaviors/actions
Variables are only for numbers; methods are only for text
There is no difference between variables and methods in a class
questions.explanation: Variables inside a class define the properties (state/data) of the object, while methods define the behaviors (actions) the object can perform.

hints.hint: Think: properties = what it knows, behaviors = what it does.

interviewQA.question: What is a class in Java?
interviewQA.expectedAnswer: A class is a user-defined blueprint or template from which individual objects are created. It defines the properties (variables) and behaviors (methods) that all objects of that type will possess.
keyPoints: Does not allocate object data in memory until an object is created
commonMistakes: Confusing a class with an object. A class is the recipe; the object is the cake.

activities.title: Lesson 3 Checkpoint
checklist: I can explain the difference between a blueprint and an actual object.
I can write a class in Java with properties and a simple method.
I understand that defining a class does not automatically create an object in memory.

practiceProblems.title: Write a Smartphone Blueprint
practiceProblems.description: Write a class named Smartphone with two properties: String brand and int batteryLevel. Add a method void ring() that prints: '[brand] phone is ringing! Battery: [batteryLevel]%'. In Main, print 'Smartphone blueprint created!'.
practiceProblems.hint: Define class Smartphone { String brand; int batteryLevel; void ring() { ... } }.
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Write a Smartphone class blueprint with brand, batteryLevel, and a ring() method.
hints: Make sure the class name is capitalized as 'Smartphone'.

practiceProblems.title: Write an Employee Blueprint
practiceProblems.description: Write an Employee class with String name, String department, and double salary. Add a method void introduce() that prints: 'Hello, I am [name] from [department]'. In Main, print 'Employee blueprint ready!'.
practiceProblems.hint: Create the 3 fields and the introduce() method inside class Employee.
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Create an Employee blueprint with name, department, salary, and an introduce() method.
hints: Keep the fields default package-private for now.
